en.headline: CUHK head calls for better intellectual property training for scientists
en.dek: Vice-Chancellor Dennis Lo said researchers should patent their work and urged the government to consider an early-stage angel fund that is not too dilutive.
body: Chinese University of Hong Kong Vice-Chancellor Dennis Lo said on Friday that Hong Kong scientists need better training on intellectual property so they can protect their research and turn it into real-world products.

Speaking on an RTHK programme, Lo said some scientists spend years on research but do not bother to patent their inventions, thinking they are simply contributing to the world. Without a patent, he warned, other companies can take the work for themselves.

Lo urged scientists to patent their discoveries and said they could always donate the rights later. He also called on universities to do more to protect researchers and help them understand their rights, and on scientists to learn to spot unfair terms when accepting funding.

He highlighted the value of a government-backed fund that does not take too large a stake, allowing inventors to gain commercial experience before entering the open market. Lo suggested the government consider setting up an early-stage angel fund that is not too dilutive so inventors do not lose their rights too early and can explore commercialisation for a year or two.

zh.headline: 中大校長促加強科研人員知識產權培訓
zh.dek: 盧煜明表示科學家應為研究成果申請專利，並建議政府考慮設立不太攤薄股權的早期天使基金。
body: 香港中文大學校長盧煜明周五表示，本港科學家需要更好的知識產權培訓，以保障研究並將成果轉化為實際產品。
他在香港電台節目中指出，部分科學家花多年時間研究卻不申請專利，以為只是在為世界作出貢獻；但若沒有專利，其他公司可直接取用有關成果。
盧煜明呼籲科學家為發明申請專利，並表示日後仍可捐出權利。他亦促請大學加強保障科研人員及協助他們了解自身權利，同時建議研究人員在接受資助時留意不公平條款。
他提到政府支援基金若持股比例不高，可讓發明人先累積商業經驗才進入公開市場。盧煜明建議政府可考慮設立不太攤薄股權的早期天使基金，讓發明人保留較多權利，並有一至兩年時間探索商業化。
